# Haohan Wang

> Haohan Wang (汪浩瀚) is an Assistant Professor in the School of Information Sciences at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC), where he leads the DREAM Lab. His research covers agentic AI for scientific discovery, computational biology, and trustworthy and secure AI (LLM jailbreaks, prompt injection, robustness).

## Key facts
- Position: Assistant Professor, School of Information Sciences, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (since 2022)
- Affiliated faculty: Siebel School of Computing and Data Science; Carl R. Woese Institute for Genomic Biology; Beckman Institute for Advanced Science and Technology; Interdisciplinary Health Sciences Institute; National Center for Supercomputing Applications
- Lab: DREAM Lab, https://dream.ischool.illinois.edu/
- Education: Ph.D. (2021) and M.S. (2015), Language Technologies Institute, Carnegie Mellon University (Ph.D. advisor: Eric P. Xing)
- Previously: Postdoctoral Researcher, Machine Learning Department, Carnegie Mellon University (2022)
- Selected recognition: Next Generation in Biomedicine, Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard (2019); Rising Star in AI+X, Baidu Research (2022); Best Paper Honorable Mention, WSDM 2023; Outstanding Paper Award, FL@FM Workshop at NeurIPS 2024; Student Paper Award, IEEE BIBM 2017
- Service: General Chair, Midwest Machine Learning Symposium 2026; Area Chair for NeurIPS, ICML, and ACL; Editor for Scientific Reports and TMLR
- Contact: haohanw@illinois.edu

## Research areas
- Agentic AI: multi-agent LLM systems that automate complex data analysis, e.g. virtual bioinformaticians for gene expression analysis (GenoMAS, GenoTEX); efficient test-time scaling and multi-agent building blocks
- Computational biology: gene regulatory network inference from spatial and single-cell transcriptomics; genetic basis of Alzheimer's disease and other complex traits
- Trustworthy and secure AI: ranking and visibility in LLM-based search (CORE), LLM jailbreak attacks and defenses (e.g. InfoFlood, cipher-character jailbreaks), prompt-injection defense, content-moderation guardrails, robust and generalizable machine learning

## Speaking and collaboration
Haohan Wang is available to give keynotes, invited talks, seminars, tutorials, and panel discussions (in person or virtual) for academic, industry, and policy audiences; to invite him, email haohanw@illinois.edu. He has given nearly 50 invited talks and tutorials on agentic AI for biomedical discovery, LLM jailbreaks and prompt-injection defense, spatial gene regulation and disease genetics, and trustworthy machine learning. Past hosts include NIH/NLM, NIH NIDA, the NAIRR Pilot, Stanford, Tsinghua University, EMBL-EBI, the Broad Institute, Capital One, and KDD (tutorial). He welcomes collaborations in three areas: agentic AI (multi-agent architectures, efficient test-time scaling, AI scientists for discovery), trustworthy and secure AI (jailbreaks and red teaming, prompt-injection defense, ranking and visibility in LLM-based search), and computational biology (agentic analysis of thousands of diseases, spatial and single-cell gene regulation, shared genetic architecture of Alzheimer's disease, autism, and other complex diseases). Contact: haohanw@illinois.edu.

## Pages
- [Homepage](https://haohanwang.ischool.illinois.edu/): bio, research, news, invited talks, awards, teaching, service
- [Agentic AI for Genomics](https://haohanwang.ischool.illinois.edu/research/agentic-ai-genomics.html): LLM agents as virtual bioinformaticians (GenoMAS, GenoTEX), key results, talks
- [LLM Security](https://haohanwang.ischool.illinois.edu/research/llm-security.html): jailbreaks (InfoFlood, cipher characters, self-jailbreaking, audio attacks) and prompt-injection defense
- [Visibility in LLM-Based Search](https://haohanwang.ischool.illinois.edu/research/llm-search-visibility.html): how generative engines rank and recommend content; CORE method and ProductBench benchmark
- [Gene Regulation & Disease Genetics](https://haohanwang.ischool.illinois.edu/research/gene-regulation-disease-genetics.html): spatial gene regulatory networks (SVGRN), Alzheimer's disease genetics (Het-PR), KMM
- [Blog](https://haohanwang.ischool.illinois.edu/blog/): personal perspectives on AI research (structured vision/SVG, a unified view of trustworthy AI, evaluating prompt-injection defenses)
